findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Oversized animated GIFs with extensionless upload temp paths select convert[0] and permanently lose animation even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Replacing the type-specific configured limit with 10 MB changes the attachment upload contract too, so attachments valid under a higher max_attachment_size_kb are now rejected by the concrete validateUploadedFiles caller.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Each oversized upload can run up to five full ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes, multiplying upload-worker CPU use and latency under concurrent uploads.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Each oversized upload can run up to five image-conversion subprocesses without a timeout, so a stuck conversion can indefinitely occupy deferred-upload workers and prevent completion notifications.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — No upload test exercises an actual oversized image through the new in-place conversion loop and verifies the bytes fall below the configured limit before Upload.create_for, so converter failures and ineffective repeated downsizing can ship while the core feature remains broken.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Oversized animated GIFs with extensionless upload temp paths select convert[0] and permanently lose animation even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the diff, in uploads_controller.rb:67, the code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In optimized_image.rb, the `optimize` method checks `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` to determine if it should use animated instructions. However, tempfile paths (like `/tmp/discourse-upload-xxx`) don't have a .GIF extension, so this regex will never match for temp files. This means animated GIFs will be processed with non-animated instructions (convert[0] which takes only the first frame), permanently losing animation even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Capping API URL downloads at 10 MB breaks clients on sites configured above 10 MB, where previously valid URL uploads now fail before they can be reduced to the configured image limit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 55 changes from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` for API URL downloads. If a site has configured max_image_size_kb to be greater than 10MB (10240 KB), the download will now be capped at 10MB instead of the configured limit. The subsequent downsizing loop (lines 63-68) reduces images to `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but if the configured limit is above 10MB, the download itself will fail/truncate before the image can be processed. This is a real behavioral regression for sites configured with limits above 10MB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The unconditional 10 MB limit rejects attachments previously allowed by a larger max_attachment_size_kb setting even though only images can be downsized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 182 changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). The original code used dynamic settings based on 'type' which could be 'attachment' or 'image'. The finding correctly identifies that this hardcoded 10MB limit would reject attachments that were previously allowed if max_attachment_size_kb was set higher than 10MB. The server-side downsizing logic only applies to images (checked via `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`), so non-image attachments cannot be downsized and would simply be rejected at the client-side validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Each oversized upload can run up to five full ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes, multiplying upload-worker CPU use and latency under concurrent uploads.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new code at lines 63-68 in uploads_controller.rb introduces a loop that can run up to 5 iterations of OptimizedImage.downsize() for each oversized image upload. This is a legitimate performance/scalability concern - each iteration involves ImageMagick processing, and under concurrent uploads this could significantly increase CPU load and latency. The code is clearly visible in the diff: 'attempt = 5' followed by 'while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes' calling OptimizedImage.downsize. This is not a bug (the code works as intended) but is a valid architectural/performance concern about the new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Each oversized upload can run up to five image-conversion subprocesses without a timeout, so a stuck conversion can indefinitely occupy deferred-upload workers and prevent completion notifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new loop at lines 63-67 that calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to 5 times. Looking at the downsize method in optimized_image.rb, it calls optimize() which eventually runs `convert_with` that executes a shell command via backticks without any timeout mechanism. The finding correctly identifies that these subprocess calls have no timeout, and if a conversion hangs, it would block the worker indefinitely. This is a real defect in the new code - the loop can run up to 5 image conversions with no timeout protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — No upload test exercises an actual oversized image through the new in-place conversion loop and verifies the bytes fall below the configured limit before Upload.create_for, so converter failures and ineffective repeated downsizing can ship while the core feature remains broken.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial logic at lines 63-69 in uploads_controller.rb - a loop that attempts to downsize images up to 5 times until they fall below the configured limit. This is significant new functionality that could fail silently (the loop might not effectively reduce file size, or OptimizedImage.downsize could fail). The finding correctly identifies that there's no test coverage shown in the diff for this new conversion loop, which is a legitimate concern for newly added complex logic. This is a valid 'missing test for new nontrivial logic' issue, not a bug or hallucination.
